definition: An invariant feature is a detectable pattern in an image that remains recognizable even when the target changes in position or orientation, which makes it useful for recognition and tracking across motion or rotation.

reasons: The packet only supports rotation invariance for SIFT features, not the broader claim that the feature remains recognizable when the target changes in position as well as orientation.

The packet supports use in target recognition and tracking, but it does not establish the general definition of an “invariant feature” as a detectable image pattern with that behavior across motion or rotation.

The packet does not provide a definition or direct support for the term “invariant feature” itself; it discusses SIFT features and claims about SIFT’s rotation invariance, but it does not define what an “invariant feature” is in general cognition terms.

The definition’s phrasing (“detectable pattern in an image,” “remains recognizable”) is not explicitly stated in the packet; support is indirect via SIFT being used for recognition/tracking and described as invariant to rotation.
